title: Record quarters at TSMC and Samsung, and a US source for interposers
intro: TSMC's third-quarter revenue rose 50% and Samsung guided to a near ninefold jump in operating profit, both on AI demand, while GlobalFoundries signed a $2B deal to make CoWoS silicon interposers in New York from 2028. An OpenAI revenue figure below what had circulated knocked NVIDIA, Oracle and CoreWeave on Oct 8, and Lumentum said its optical capacity is booked into 2029.
movers_note: On the 46 companies with a new quote since Oct 7, the biggest declines were Astera Labs −10.7%, Arm −9.3%, SK hynix −8.7%, Supermicro −8.1%; the biggest gains were Wiwynn +7.4%, GlobalFoundries +2.7%, Tokyo Electron +1.6%, Synopsys +1.1%.

items.headline: OpenAI's ~$50B revenue run-rate, below the ~$68B that had circulated, hits AI-infrastructure stocks
items.summary: The end-September figure became public on Oct 8; the gap reflects gross-versus-net counting of cloud-partner sales rather than lost business. NVIDIA, Oracle and CoreWeave sold off and the Nasdaq 100 fell about 1.4%, before chips steadied on Oct 9 after Bloomberg reported OpenAI still expects at least $70B annualized by year-end.

items.headline: TSMC books record Q3 revenue of NT$1.49T, up 50% and above its guidance
items.summary: September sales of NT$511.9B rose 54.6% year over year, putting Q3 at about $46.7B against guidance of $44.6-45.8B. Nine-month revenue reached NT$3.90T, up 41%, ahead of the Oct 15 earnings call.

items.headline: GlobalFoundries wins a $2B, five-year TSMC deal to make CoWoS silicon interposers in New York
items.summary: GF will make silicon interposers with embedded deep-trench capacitors for TSMC's CoWoS ecosystem at its Malta, New York fab, with volume ramp planned for the first half of 2028. It would be the first US-based source of a packaging input that has limited AI accelerator output.

items.headline: Samsung guides Q3 operating profit to about KRW 107T, nearly nine times a year ago
items.summary: Preliminary figures show about KRW 195T of sales and KRW 107.4T of operating profit, a fourth straight record driven by memory while mobile lost money and foundry stayed unprofitable. TrendForce expects Q4 conventional DRAM contract prices up 10-15%, a slower rise than Q2's.

items.headline: Lumentum says optical component capacity is booked through early 2029
items.summary: CEO Michael Hurlston told Bloomberg that Lumentum may be unable to fill as much as 70% of 2027 demand for most products, a tighter outlook than six months ago. Optical names rose on Oct 9, with Lumentum up more than 6% and Coherent about 5%.

items.headline: Marvell sets a fiscal-2031 revenue target of $70-90B and lifts fiscal 2028 to $20B
items.summary: Management tied the extra $2B in fiscal 2028 to data-center connectivity such as scale-up optics and switching, alongside custom AI chips for hyperscalers including Amazon and Google. Shares rose about 4%, with Astera Labs up 8% and Credo up 6%.

items.headline: AMD's Lisa Su, touring Taiwan and Korea, promises substantially more CPU and GPU supply in 2027
items.summary: Su said AMD is planning three to five years ahead, needs more advanced wafer capacity, and is working closely with memory makers to secure supply; she met Foxconn and was due to see TSMC before visiting Korea. Leading-edge wafers and HBM remain the binding constraints on accelerator output.

items.headline: Intel stays in Musk's Terafab on 14A; Musk rejects TSMC takeover talk and floats a cleanroom sublease
items.summary: Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan told Bloomberg that Intel remains part of the SpaceX, Tesla and xAI-backed fab effort built around its 14A process. Musk said Terafab will build and run the fab itself and that TSMC could at most sublease part of it, leaving TSMC's role unclear.

items.headline: Black Hills signs through-2048 deals to power Google's Cheyenne data center with a 2.7 GW resource mix
items.summary: The package covers up to 590 MW of grid-connected service, including 564 MW of new gas generation costing $1.8B over 2027-29, plus about 2.1 GW of third-party resources run through a private microgrid. Service begins in late 2027 and peaks in 2030, with Google bearing the costs.

items.headline: Quanta's September revenue hits a record NT$325B as Vera Rubin servers enter trial production
items.summary: Revenue rose 76.7% year over year but fell 23% from an unusually high August, which management attributed to shipment timing; Q3 totaled about NT$1.12T, up 125%. GB300 output is on schedule, with Vera Rubin shipping in small volumes in Q4 and ramping in Q1.

items.headline: AWS raises reserved GPU Capacity Block prices about 15%; Trainium reservations unchanged
items.summary: Reserved NVIDIA GPU rates rose roughly 15% on Oct 7, putting a B300 near $16.15 per accelerator-hour, while on-demand, savings-plan and Trainium reservation prices were left unchanged. AWS says the rates float with supply and demand.

items.headline: BofA downgrades Besi as ASML's interest in hybrid bonding raises competitive risk
items.summary: Bank of America cut Besi to neutral and roughly halved its target, arguing ASML's exploration of hybrid bonding could weigh on the stock until its plans are clearer. Besi, the leading hybrid-bonder supplier, remains up about 45% this year but roughly 40% below its June peak.
